summary: Rearrange nums into the next lexicographically greater permutation in place (or the smallest if none).
mainInsight: Scan from the right for the first index i with nums[i] < nums[i+1] (the pivot). Swap it with the smallest larger element to its right (found from the right since the suffix is non-increasing), then reverse the suffix after i to make it the smallest.

approaches.name: Pivot, swap, reverse
approaches.summary: Find pivot, swap with next larger from the right, reverse the tail.

commonMistakes: Choosing the first larger element from the left instead of the right
Using >= vs > when looking for the pivot with duplicates

promptVariants: What are the three steps of the next-permutation algorithm?
How do you transform the array into the next permutation in place?
options: Find the rightmost ascent, swap with the next larger on its right, reverse the suffix
Sort the suffix descending, then swap the first two items
Reverse the whole array, then swap the last two items
Swap the two largest items, then sort everything again
cards.answer: Find the rightmost ascent, swap with the next larger on its right, reverse the suffix
cards.explanation: The suffix right of the pivot is non-increasing, so reversing it makes it the smallest possible.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Sort the suffix descending, then swap th: That does not produce the next permutation.

promptVariants: Why is the suffix after the pivot in non-increasing order, and why is reversing it enough?
Why do we swap with the smallest larger element?
cards.answer: The pivot is the rightmost ascent, so everything to its right is non-increasing, i.e. already the largest arrangement of that suffix. Swapping the pivot with the smallest larger element increases the prefix minimally, and the suffix (still non-increasing after the swap) is then reversed into ascending order, which is the smallest arrangement.
keyPoints: Smallest larger element keeps the increase minimal
cards.explanation: That gives the very next permutation.
One scan for the pivot, one for the swap target, one reverse.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
cards.explanation: The array is modified in place.

promptVariants: What does the algorithm do for [3, 2, 1]?
options: No pivot exists, so the whole array is reversed to [1, 2, 3]
It raises an error because no larger permutation exists
It swaps the first and last elements only to [1, 2, 3]
cards.answer: No pivot exists, so the whole array is reversed to [1, 2, 3]
cards.explanation: When the array is entirely non-increasing it is the last permutation, so it wraps to the first.

incorrectOptionExplanations.It raises an error because no larger per: The problem asks for the smallest permutation instead.
incorrectOptionExplanations.It returns the array unchanged: The wrap-around must produce ascending order.
incorrectOptionExplanations.It swaps the first and last elements onl: That only works by accident for length 3.
